evals.prompt: I want to find all accounts that are within 3 hops of any flagged fraud node in my transaction graph. Show me the GFQL chain-list syntax.
evals.expected_output: Shows g.gfql([n({'flagged': True}), e_forward(min_hops=1, max_hops=3), n()]) or equivalent chain-list pattern

assertions.text: Uses e_forward() with min_hops/max_hops or equivalent
Does not use deprecated hop() or chain() methods

evals.prompt: Can I write a Cypher query to find people who know someone over 30 years old in my PyGraphistry graph?
evals.expected_output: Shows g.gfql("MATCH (p:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(q) WHERE q.age > 30 RETURN p.name") or equivalent. Explains label__Person column mapping if needed.

assertions.text: Uses g.gfql() with a Cypher string argument
Shows WHERE clause with property filter
Mentions label__Person column mapping or recommends WHERE p.type='Person' as simpler alternative

evals.prompt: How do I use Let bindings in GFQL to define reusable subgraph patterns as named variables?
evals.expected_output: Shows Let/DAG binding syntax with named pattern variables, explains scoping rules, gives a concrete example

assertions.text: Shows Let binding or DAG variable syntax in GFQL
Includes a concrete example with named pattern variable

evals.prompt: How do I change the color of nodes in my PyGraphistry plot based on a 'category' column?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT stay in pygraphistry-gfql; this is a visualization task and routes to pygraphistry-visualization for encode_point_color

assertions.text: Routes to pygraphistry-visualization for color encoding
Does not answer the styling question with GFQL syntax
